chunk_findings.detail: The fake report is constructed as `A.FamilyReport("alpha", ("a",), ("home",), ("home", "stray"))`. `FamilyReport`'s positional order is `(name, importers, home, violations)`, so `_ratchet_gaps` reads `("home", "stray")` from `actual["alpha"].violations`. Against the empty baseline `{"alpha": ()}` that makes `grew == ["home", "stray"]`, not `["stray"]` as asserted. The new test always fails.

The diff only changes tomllib/tomlkit homes and removes one baseline line, so the rewritten all-families assertion will still receive non-empty `grew`/`removed` for clock-env and fail the same test on main.

chunk_findings.detail: The ratchet is still red after this change. Declaring `tomllib`’s home and dropping `ddflow.infra.fsio` from the shutil baseline does not cover the drift measured on main: shutil still has other new importers, and clock-env still has the ~35 new importers (including `ddflow.adapters.notify` and `ddflow.services.meters`) plus the stale baseline entries. `STD_LIB_HOMES` / `THIRD_PARTY_HOMES` are not updated for clock, env, entropy, or the package splits, and no importer was moved onto its home. `test_ratchet_violations_match_baseline` therefore still fails on that census, so B068d551e89 is not closed.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_arch_deps.py:test_ratchet_violations_match_baseline

chunk_findings.detail: `_ratchet_gaps` indexes `actual[name]` for every baseline family and never records families present only in the baseline. Given `actual={"alpha": FamilyReport(...violations=("stray",))}` and `baseline={"alpha": (), "clock-env": ("ddflow.adapters.notify",)}`, the loop raises `KeyError: "clock-env"` before returning, so the assertion never prints alpha’s growth or the missing family. That is the same “stops before naming every family” failure B068d551e89 asked the helper to eliminate.

data.probe: FamilyReport fields are (family, members, home, importers, third_party) per the @dataclass in ddflow/services/archdeps.py. A.FamilyReport('alpha',('a',),('home',),('home','stray')) => home=('home',), importers=('home','stray'), violations=importers-home=('stray',), so grew==['stray'] exactly as asserted.
